facts.statement: Nundasuchus is classified as an extinct genus of crurotarsan archosaurs, likely related to Paracrocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: Nundasuchus is an extinct genus of crurotarsan, possibly a suchian archosaur related to Paracrocodylomorpha.

facts.statement: Nundasuchus lived in what is now Tanzania, Africa, approximately 240 million years ago.
facts.quote: Nundasuchus lived in what is now Tanzania, Africa around 240 million years ago.

facts.statement: Nundasuchus was likely a carnivore possessing ziphodont, steak-knife-like teeth and rows of bony plates called osteoderms along its back.
facts.quote: Members of this genus were likely carnivores, with ziphodont (steak knife-like) teeth and rows of bony plates (osteoderms) along their back.

facts.statement: Unlike modern crocodilians, Nundasuchus had an upright stance with its legs positioned directly underneath its body.
facts.quote: Nundasuchus had an upright stance, with legs situated directly underneath the body, as with various other early pseudosuchians (such as "rauisuchians" and aetosaurs) but unlike modern crocodilians.

facts.statement: Scientists debate the exact classification of Nundasuchus relative to other pseudosuchians.
facts.quote: The classification of Nundasuchus relative to other pseudosuchians is somewhat controversial.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Nundasuchus belongs near the base of the pseudosuchian group alongside phytosaurs, citing primitive features like palate teeth and a short pubis.
facts.quote: Some phylogenetic analyses place it near or at the base of the group, sometimes along with phytosaurs, based on certain plesiomorphic (primitive) features such as teeth on the palate, a short pubis, and characteristics of the calcaneum (heel bone).

facts.statement: Another hypothesis posits that Nundasuchus is more advanced and closer to Ticinosuchus and paracrocodylomorphs, a view supported by its 2014 description.
facts.quote: Another hypothesis, supported by its original 2014 description, considers it to be somewhat more "advanced" than those groups, instead being closer to Ticinosuchus and paracrocodylomorphs (the group containing "rauisuchians" and the ancestors of modern crocodilians).

facts.statement: Nundasuchus is known only from the holotype specimen NMT RB48, a partially complete and disarticulated skeleton housed at the National Museum of Tanzania.
facts.quote: Nundasuchus is known solely from the holotype NMT RB48, a partially complete disassociated and mostly disarticulated individual housed at the National Museum of Tanzania, Dar es Salaam of Tanzania.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with South African fauna, the Nundasuchus fossil beds are dated to the Anisian stage of the early Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: Based on comparison with the better studied tetrapod fauna of Subzone C of the Cynognathus Assemblage Zone of South Africa, this member is considered to date to the Anisian stage of the early Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: Nundasuchus possessed unusual pterygoid teeth along the midline of its palate, a feature rare among archosaurs.
facts.quote: The portion of the pterygoid which would have been positioned along the midline of the palate is unusual compared to other archosaurs due to possessing teeth.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Nundasuchus expanded into heart-shaped structures at their upper front tips, a feature similar to those found in Batrachotomus.
facts.quote: Isolated cervical neural spines were similar to those of Batrachotomus, being expanded towards their upper front tips into heart-shaped structures when seen from above.

facts.statement: Most of the back vertebrae of Nundasuchus were tall, concave on both ends, and had a pair of ventral keels separated by a shallow groove.
facts.quote: Most of the dorsal (back) vertebrae were tall and amphicoelous, and possessed a pair of ventral keels adjacent to the midline, separated by a shallow groove.

facts.statement: The ventral keels on Nundasuchus are considered a unique trait among archosaurs and likely evolved convergently with the similar structures found in the unrelated aquatic archosauriform Vancleavea.
facts.quote: Considering that Nundasuchus is not closely related to Vancleavea, its ventral keels were probably an example of convergent evolution, and they can be considered a unique trait compared to other archosaurs.

facts.statement: The original description of Nundasuchus vertebrae suggested the possible presence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations.
facts.quote: One notable feature of the vertebrae of Nundasuchus is the possible presence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations, as reported by the original description.

facts.statement: A 2018 study disputed the presence of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations in Nundasuchus, arguing they were misidentified parts of the zygapophyses.
facts.quote: However, a 2018 study doubted this interpretation, arguing that the supposed articulations were actually misidentified components of the zygapophyses.

facts.statement: The second sacral rib of Nundasuchus was flatter and tilted diagonally so that its rear edge was higher than its front edge.
facts.quote: The second sacral rib is flatter, and tilts diagonally so that its tapering rear edge is positioned higher than its front edge.

facts.statement: Nundasuchus fossils include several groups of preserved osteoderms, which are plate-like bony scutes.
facts.quote: Several groups of osteoderms (plate-like bony scutes) were also preserved in Nundasuchus.

facts.statement: The thin-type osteoderms of Nundasuchus formed several longitudinal rows stretching along the animal's backbone.
facts.quote: At least the "thin"-type osteoderms formed several longitudinal rows stretching along the backbone of the animal.

facts.statement: An estimated five osteoderms were present for every two vertebrae in Nundasuchus.
facts.quote: An estimated five osteoderms were present per every two vertebrae.

facts.statement: The scapula of Nundasuchus was paddle-like and relatively small.
facts.quote: The scapula (shoulder blade) was paddle-like and somewhat small.

facts.statement: The lower edge of the Nundasuchus scapula connected to a semicircular coracoid bone.
facts.quote: The lower edge of the scapula connects to the semicircular coracoid bone.

facts.statement: A wide groove was present below the glenoid of the Nundasuchus scapula, a feature similar to that found in aetosaurs and Postosuchus.
facts.quote: However, a wide groove is present below the glenoid when seen from the side, similar to the case in aetosaurs and Postosuchus.

facts.statement: The coracoid foramen in Nundasuchus is unique because it is surrounded by several knob-like structures.
facts.quote: In front of the glenoid, a hole known as the coracoid foramen pierces the coracoid, and, in a feature unique to Nundasuchus, this hole is surrounded by several knob-like structures.

facts.statement: The only known forelimb bone of Nundasuchus is the humerus, or upper arm bone.
facts.quote: The only portion of the forelimb known for this genus was the humerus (upper arm bone).

facts.statement: The humerus of Nundasuchus had a concave medial edge and an almost straight lateral edge, similar to phytosaurs.
facts.quote: Its medial edge was concave while the lateral edge was almost straight as in phytosaurs.

facts.statement: Both the head and the lower tip of the Nundasuchus humerus were covered with deep grooves.
facts.quote: Both the humeral head and the tip of the lower extremity of the bone were covered with deep grooves.

facts.statement: The pubis bone in Nundasuchus is characteristically small, measuring only about 30% of the femur's length.
facts.quote: This bone was characteristically small in Nundasuchus, only about 30% the length of the femur.

facts.statement: The Nundasuchus femur is S-shaped, with the femoral head twisted inwards and the distal condyles twisted outwards.
facts.quote: The femur (thigh bone) is sigmoidal (S-shaped), with the femoral head being twisted slightly inwards and the distal condyles being twisted slightly outwards.

facts.statement: The twist in the Nundasuchus femur creates a 45-degree angle between its extremities, a trait shared with most eucrocopodans except dinosaurs.
facts.quote: This creates an angle of 45 degrees between these two extremities of the bone, as with most eucrocopodans apart from dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The distal part of the Nundasuchus femur features a large crista tibiofibularis, which is an upper extension of the lateral condyle.
facts.quote: The distal part of the femur has a large crista tibiofibularis, an upper extension of the lateral condyle.

facts.statement: The proximal part of the Nundasuchus tibia is roughly diamond-shaped in cross-section, featuring rounded tubera and a low, indistinct forward-pointing ridge called a cnemial crest.
facts.quote: The proximal part of the tibia (inner shin bone) is roughly diamond-shaped in cross section, with rounded lateral and medial tubera as well as a low and indistinct forward-pointing ridge known as a cnemial crest.

facts.statement: Although incomplete, metatarsal IV in Nundasuchus is estimated to be longer than metatarsal III.
facts.quote: Although metatarsal IV is incomplete, it has been estimated to be longer than III.

facts.statement: The phalanges of the fifth toe in Nundasuchus are longer and hourglass-shaped, attached to a rough-textured claw.
facts.quote: The phalanges are generally robust, but those of the fifth toe were longer and hourglass-shaped, attached to a rough-textured ungual (claw).

facts.statement: The lateral side of the calcaneal tuber in Nundasuchus has a noticeable pad that appears unique to this species.
facts.quote: The lateral side of the tuber has a noticeable 'pad', which is seemingly unique to Nundasuchus.

facts.statement: The upper surface of the Nundasuchus calcaneum connects to the fibula via a convex, barrel-shaped joint.
facts.quote: The upper surface for the calcaneum connects to the fibula with a convex, barrel-shaped joint.

facts.statement: The front edge of the Nundasuchus astragalus has a large concave surface called an astragalar hollow overlying a small convexity called an astragalar ball.
facts.quote: The front edge of the astragalus has a large concave surface (astragalar hollow) overlying a small convexity (astragalar ball).

facts.statement: Nundasuchus was first described and named by Sterling J. Nesbitt, Christian A. Sidor, Kenneth D. Angielczyk, Roger M. H. Smith, and Linda A. Tsuji in 2014.
facts.quote: Nundasuchus was first described and named by Sterling J. Nesbitt, Christian A. Sidor, Kenneth D. Angielczyk, Roger M. H. Smith and Linda A. Tsuji in 2014

facts.statement: The estimated length of metatarsal IV being longer than metatarsal III is highly unusual among Triassic reptiles, a trait shared only with Proterosuchus.
facts.quote: This would be highly unusual among Triassic reptiles, of which only Proterosuchus shares this characteristic.

facts.statement: Fossils of Nundasuchus come from the Manda Beds of the Middle Triassic in southwest Tanzania.
facts.quote: Los restos de este género provienen de los Lechos Manda del Triásico Medio en el suroeste de Tanzania.

facts.statement: Nundasuchus lived in what is now Tanzania, Africa, about 240 million years ago.

facts.statement: Only one species, Nundasuchus songeaensis, is known from a single partial skeleton containing vertebrae, limb elements, osteoderms, and skull fragments.
facts.quote: Solo se conoce a una especie, Nundasuchus songeaensis, conocido a partir de un único esqueleto parcial, que incluye vértebras, elementos de las extremidades, osteodermos y fragmentos del cráneo.

facts.statement: Members of this genus were likely carnivores with ziphodont (knife-shaped) teeth and rows of bony plates (osteoderms) along their backs.
facts.quote: Los miembros de este género eran probablemente carnívoros, con dientes zifodontes (en forma de cuchillo) y filas de placas óseas (osteodermos) a lo largo de su espalda.

facts.statement: Nundasuchus had an upright posture with legs positioned directly under its body, unlike modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Nundasuchus tenía una postura erguida, con patas situadas directamente bajo su cuerpo, como otros pseudosuquios primitivos (tales como los "rauisuquios" y aetosaurios) pero a diferencia de los crocodilianos modernos.

facts.statement: Many studies consider Nundasuchus a pseudosuchian, meaning it was more closely related to modern crocodilians than to dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Muchos estudios lo consideran también un pseudosuquio, lo que significa que estaba más cercanamente relacionado con los actuales crocodilianos que a los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Nundasuchus is a basal pseudosuchian with convergent traits or an archosauriform closely related to Archosauria with convergent features.
facts.quote: Therefore, it is not clear whether Nundasuchus is a suchian that has convergences with far more basal archosaurs as the two phylogenetic analyses suggest, or an archosauriform closely related to Archosauria, with features convergent to the morphology of the more advanced paracrocodylomorphs.

facts.statement: Nesbitt (2011) considered crocodylomorphs to be descended from taxa traditionally identified as "rauisuchians".
facts.quote: Nesbitt (2011) considered crocodylomorphs (crocodilian ancestors) to have been descended from taxa traditionally identified as "rauisuchians".

facts.statement: One hypothesis, supported by its 2014 description, considers Nundasuchus to be more "advanced" than basal groups rather than closer to Ticinosuchus and paracrocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: Otra hipótesis, apoyada por su descripción original de 2014, considera que era algo más "avanzado" que esos grupos, en lugar de ser más cercano a Ticinosuchus y los paracrocodilomorfos (el grupo que abarca a los "rauisuquios" y los ancestros de los crocodilianos modernos).

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses place Nundasuchus at the base of the group, sometimes with phytosaurs, based on plesiomorphic traits such as palatal teeth, a short pubis, and certain calcaneal characteristics.
facts.quote: Algunos análisis filogenéticos lo sitúa en la base de este grupo, a veces junto con los fitosaurios, basándose en ciertos rasgos plesiomórficos (primitivos) tales como los dientes en el paladar, un pubis corto, y ciertas características del calcáneo (hueso del talón).
